title: Saving and compound interest
examples: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
If I save money now, how does time help me?
Can you show me how the rule of 72 works?

explain.say: Today we learn about compound interest. It means earning interest on your interest.
Let us look at a simple example. If you save one hundred pounds, you earn interest. Next year, you earn interest on the original one hundred pounds plus the interest you already made.
Another key idea is starting early. The sooner you start saving, the more time your money has to grow. Time is very important for your savings.
We can use the rule of seventy-two. This rule helps estimate how long it takes money to double. You divide seventy-two by the interest rate percentage for an estimate.
In real life, think about a bank savings account. If the bank offers a small interest rate, your money grows slowly at first. But over many years, the interest on the interest makes a big difference.
A common mistake is thinking interest is always added to the original amount only. Remember, compound interest adds interest to the growing total each time.

faq.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
faq.a: Simple interest is only calculated on the initial amount you invested. Compound interest is calculated on the initial amount plus all the accumulated interest.
asks: Does compound interest use the original money only?
How is compound interest different from simple interest?

faq.q: Does the interest rate matter more than the time period?
faq.a: Both the interest rate and the time period are very important. A higher rate or more time will make your money grow much faster.
asks: Is time more important than the rate?
Which factor helps saving more: time or interest?

faq.q: How accurate is the rule of seventy-two?
faq.a: The rule of seventy-two is a quick estimate, not an exact calculation. It gives you a very good idea of how long it might take to double your money.
asks: Can I use 72 to guess how long it takes to double?

faq.q: Does this only apply to banks?
faq.a: No, the concept applies anywhere you earn interest. It can be from investments or other savings methods.
asks: Do I need a bank to use this?
Is this just for bank savings accounts?

faq.q: If I save a little bit every month, does it help?
faq.a: Yes, saving regularly is very helpful. Even small, consistent amounts add up greatly over a long period of time.
asks: Should I save a little bit every month?
Does saving small amounts work with compound interest?

facts: Compound interest means earning interest on previous interest.
Time is one of the most powerful tools in saving money.
The rule of seventy-two estimates doubling time by dividing 72 by the rate.
Interest rates are usually shown as a percentage.

quiz.say: If you invest money and the interest is calculated on the original amount only, this is called:
quiz.why: This is correct because simple interest only uses the starting amount for calculation.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it sounds like growth, but it is wrong because it includes interest on interest.
wrong.1: This is wrong because it is a general term and does not describe the specific method of interest calculation.
wrong.2: This is wrong because a fixed rate describes the percentage, not the method of compounding.

quiz.say: To estimate how many years it takes for your money to double at an interest rate of six percent, you should calculate:
quiz.why: The rule of seventy-two tells us to divide seventy-two by the rate, giving twelve years.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you should be dividing, not multiplying by the rate.
wrong.2: This is a common mistake of dividing by the number itself instead of using the rule.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you must divide the number by the rate, not just use the number.

quiz.say: If you save money for a long time, the interest you earn on the interest will cause your savings to:

options.show: Stop growing after the first year
options.say: Stop growing after the first year

quiz.why: This is correct because compounding means the growth accelerates as the base amount increases.

wrong.1: This describes simple interest, which does not accelerate its growth.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the interest keeps compounding year after year.
wrong.3: This is wrong because interest, by definition, adds value to your savings.
